name: Gladstonian liberalism
summary: Gladstonian liberalism is the creed of W. E. Gladstone and the Liberal party he led: financial rectitude, free trade, retrenchment and low taxation, with liberty balanced by community, a Christian humanitarianism in home and foreign affairs, gradual reform, local self-government and Irish Home Rule, and a foreign policy of international law, arbitration and the Concert of Europe.
scope: Gladstone's mature Liberalism as the scholarship describes it (Biagini and Bebbington in the Journal of Liberal History), with his 1853 budget and 1888 Home Rule speeches as primary texts. It excludes his youthful Conservative views and later New Liberal social reform. The scholars note tensions (Irish coercion in 1881-85, the invasion of Egypt in 1882), so doctrine and government record are kept apart.
